results.title: The set of commuting probabilities is closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Pr(G)$ denote the commuting probability of a group $G$: $\Pr(G) = |\{(x, y) \in G \times G : xy = yx\}| / |G|^2$ if $G$ is finite, and $\Pr(G) = 0$ if $G$ is infinite. Then the set $\{\Pr(G) : G \text{ a group}\}$ is a closed subset of $\mathbb{R}$.

results.title: Protasov's question on absolutely dense partitions (Kourovka 13.47)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every countable abelian group $G$ with only finitely many elements of order $2$ can be partitioned into two disjoint sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ with $A_1 \cup A_2 = G$ such that $A_1$ and $A_2$ are both dense in every non-discrete Hausdorff group topology on $G$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 13.47 has a positive answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every countable abelian group $G$ with only finitely many elements of order $2$ can be partitioned into two disjoint sets $A_1$ and $A_2$ with $A_1 \cup A_2 = G$ such that $A_1$ and $A_2$ are both dense in every non-discrete Hausdorff group topology on $G$.

results.title: Expansive sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a topological space $G$, a sequence $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of finite subsets of $G$ is expansive if the sets $F_n$ are pairwise disjoint and for every nonempty open set $U \subseteq G$ there is $m \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $F_n$ meets $U$ for all $n > m$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 15.80: dense partitions and expansive sequences
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every topological group $G$ admitting a sequence $(P_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint dense subsets with union $G$ has an expansive sequence.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 15.80 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that every topological group $G$ admitting a sequence $(P_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint dense subsets with union $G$ has an expansive sequence, that is, a sequence $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of $G$ such that every nonempty open set $U \subseteq G$ meets $F_n$ for all $n$ larger than some $m$.

results.title: Absolutely irreducible representations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A representation $\rho$ of a group $G$ on a vector space $V$ over a field $k$ is absolutely irreducible when $V \neq 0$, the only $G$-invariant subspaces of $V$ are $0$ and $V$, and every $k$-linear endomorphism of $V$ commuting with $\rho(g)$ for all $g \in G$ is a scalar multiple of the identity.

results.title: Mazurov's question on first cohomology (Kourovka 16.55)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every field $k$, every finite group $G$ and every faithful absolutely irreducible representation $\rho$ of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$, the first cohomology group $H^1(G, V)$ has dimension at most $2$ over $k$.

results.title: Mazurov's question on first cohomology (Kourovka 16.55) has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a field $k$, a finite group $G$ and a faithful absolutely irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $V$ such that the first cohomology group $H^1(G, V)$ has dimension greater than $2$ over $k$.

results.title: Partial derivatives commute with coefficient lifting

results.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The operator derivative is the operator of the derivative plus the lifted `O i`.

results.title: Partial sums of the exponential of a coefficient operator
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Partial operator exponential as a sum of function iterates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The finite exponential sum agrees with the source's function-iterate formula.

results.title: Formal exponential of a coefficient operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The formal exponential: coefficient `d` uses operator iterates `n ≤ d.degree`.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The defining iteration bound is exactly the source constructor's bound.

results.title: Coefficients of the operator exponential via partial sums

results.title: The operator exponential preserves the constant coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The formal exponential preserves every constant coefficient, including nonzero ones.

results.title: Operator exponential when the square of the operator vanishes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the second operator iterate vanishes on `f`, its exponential is `f + 𝒪 f`.

results.title: The operator exponential fixes series annihilated by the operator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The exponential fixes an input annihilated by the coefficient operator.

results.title: Exponential of the zero coefficient-operator family is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The exponential of the zero coefficient-map family is the identity linear map.

results.title: Lifted coefficient maps commute with coefficient-operator iterates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A lifted coefficient map commutes with every coefficient-operator iterate when the coefficient maps commute pairwise.

results.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient-operator iterate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partial derivative of the `(n + 1)`st coefficient-operator iterate is the iterate of the partial derivative plus `(n + 1)` copies of the lifted coefficient map.

results.title: Partial derivative of partial sums of the operator exponential
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partial derivative of the first `N + 1` exponential terms is the corresponding partial sum on the derivative plus the first `N` terms on the lifted coefficient map.

results.title: Partial derivative of a coefficient-operator exponential
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The partial derivative of a formal coefficient-operator exponential is the exponential of the input derivative plus the exponential of the lifted coefficient map.

results.title: Gradient law for the exponential of commuting coefficient derivations

results.title: The exponential of coefficient derivations is multiplicative

results.title: The exponential of coefficient derivations preserves one

results.summary: The formal exponential of a family of coefficient derivations preserves one.

results.title: A numerical criterion for a prime divisor of $\binom{N}{r}$ above $r$ when $N \ge 3r$
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $N$ and $r$ be natural numbers with $r \ge 4$ and $3r \le N$, and let $e = r + \lfloor \sqrt{N} \rfloor + \lfloor N^{1/3} \rfloor \cdot \lfloor \log_2 N \rfloor$. If $r \cdot 2^r \cdot (3r)^r \cdot 4^e < 3^r \cdot 4^r \cdot N^r$, then some prime $p$ with $r < p$ divides $\binom{N}{r}$.

results.title: Partial density
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, let $S, A \subseteq \beta$ and $b \in \beta$, and write $A_{\lt b} = \{x \in A \mid x < b\}$. The partial density of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$ is the proportion $\lvert S \cap A_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A_{\lt b} \rvert$ of elements of $A_{\lt b}$ that lie in $S$, taken to be $0$ when $A_{\lt b}$ is empty. By default $A = \beta$.

results.title: Upper density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The upper density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit superior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.

results.title: Lower density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The lower density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit inferior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.

results.title: Density of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, let $S, A \subseteq \beta$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, and write $\beta_{\lt b} = \{x \in \beta \mid x < b\}$. The set $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$ if the partial density $\lvert S \cap A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert$, taken to be $0$ when the denominator is $0$, tends to $\alpha$ as…

results.title: Positive density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The set $S$ has positive density relative to $A$ if there is a real number $\alpha > 0$ such that $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$. By default $A = \beta$.

results.title: Two-sided partial density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $S$ of integers and a natural number $N$, the two-sided partial natural density of $S$ at $N$ is $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.

results.title: Two-sided natural density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S$ of integers has two-sided natural density $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$ tends to $\alpha$ as the natural number $N$ tends to infinity, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.

results.title: The whole order has density one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\beta$ be a partial order with a least element and at least two elements, in which every closed interval $[a, b]$ is finite. Then the set of all elements of $\beta$ has density $1$ (relative to all of $\beta$).

results.title: Natural density of the even numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The set of even natural numbers has natural density $1/2$.

results.title: Finite sets have natural density zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite set of natural numbers has natural density $0$.

results.title: Sets of nonzero natural density are infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a set $S$ of natural numbers has natural density $\alpha$ with $\alpha \neq 0$, then $S$ is infinite.

results.title: Logarithmic density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A$ of natural numbers has logarithmic density $d \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\frac{1}{\log n} \sum_{k \in A,\, k \le n} \frac{1}{k}$ tends to $d$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm, the term $1/k$ for $k = 0$ is taken to be $0$, and the whole expression is taken to be $0$ when $\log n = 0$.

results.title: Total arc length of a knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$, the total arc length of $K$ is the arc length of $K$ between the parameters $0$ and $2\pi$, namely $\left| \int_0^{2\pi} \lVert \gamma'(u) \rVert \, du \right|$.

results.title: Intrinsic distance on a knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a knot $K$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, let $\ell$ be the arc length of $K$ between the parameters $s$ and $t$, and let $L$ be the total arc length of $K$. The intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ is $\min(\ell, L - \ell)$. When $s$ and $t$ lie in one closed interval of length $2\pi$, this is the length of the shorter of the two arcs of $K$ joining the points with parameters $s$ and $t$.

results.title: Distortion ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma$ and real numbers $s$ and $t$, the distortion ratio of $K$ at $s$ and $t$ is the intrinsic distance between $s$ and $t$ along $K$ divided by the Euclidean distance $\lVert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rVert$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, where division by $0$ gives $0$.

results.title: Distortion of a knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a knot $K$, the distortion of $K$ is the supremum in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ of the distortion ratios of $K$ at $s$ and $t$, taken over all distinct parameters $s \ne t$ in the half-open interval $[0, 2\pi)$.

results.title: Standard torus curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $p$ and $q$, the standard $(p, q)$-torus curve is the map $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ sending $t$ to $((2 + \cos qt) \cos pt,\ (2 + \cos qt) \sin pt,\ \sin qt)$. It lies on the torus of revolution about the $z$-axis with major radius $2$ and minor radius $1$, and as $t$ runs over $[0, 2\pi]$ it winds $p$ times around the $z$-axis and $q$ times around the core circle of the torus.

results.title: A symmetric linear map from a Banach space to its dual is bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space with dual space $E^*$ of continuous linear functionals, and let $T : E \to E^*$ be a linear map that is symmetric: $(Tx)(y) = (Ty)(x)$ for all $x, y \in E$. Then $T$ is bounded: there is a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $\|Tx\| \le C \|x\|$ for all $x \in E$, where $\|Tx\|$ is the operator norm of the functional $Tx$.

results.title: Bartle–Graves theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ and $F$ be real Banach spaces and let $T : E \to F$ be a surjective continuous linear map. Then there are a continuous map $g : F \to E$, in general not linear, and a constant $C \ge 0$ such that $T(g(y)) = y$ for every $y \in F$, $g(0) = 0$, $g(t y) = t \, g(y)$ for every real $t \ge 0$ and every $y \in F$, and $\|g(y)\| \le C \|y\|$ for every $y \in F$.

results.title: Lomonosov's invariant subspace theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space, let $K$ be a nonzero compact operator on $E$, and let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on $E$ with $TK = KT$. Then there is a closed linear subspace $M$ of $E$ with $M \ne \{0\}$ and $M \ne E$ that is invariant under $T$: $T x \in M$ for every $x \in M$.

results.title: Catalan's constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Catalan's constant is the real number $G = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2}$.

results.title: The series for Catalan's constant converges absolutely
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2}$ converges absolutely: its terms are bounded in absolute value by $\frac{1}{(n+1)^2}$, and $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1}{(n+1)^2}$ converges.

results.title: Catalan's constant as a series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Catalan's constant $G$ equals $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2}$.

results.title: The series for Catalan's constant converges to it
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{(2n+1)^2}$ converges unconditionally, and its sum is Catalan's constant $G$.

results.title: Partition polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a partition $\lambda$ of a natural number $n$ with parts $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\ell$, listed with multiplicity, the (unnormalized) partition polynomial of $\lambda$ is $f_\lambda(x) = x^{\lambda_1} + \dots + x^{\lambda_\ell}$, a polynomial with natural number coefficients.

results.title: Coefficients of the partition polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $\lambda$ of a natural number $n$ and every $j \in \mathbb{N}$, the coefficient of $x^j$ in the partition polynomial $f_\lambda$ equals the number of parts of $\lambda$ equal to $j$.

results.title: The partition polynomial at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every partition $\lambda$ of a natural number $n$, the value $f_\lambda(1)$ of the partition polynomial $f_\lambda$ at $1$ equals the number of parts of $\lambda$, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Vertices joined to two vertices of a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex type $V$ and let $T$ and $Y$ be finite sets of vertices. The set $Y$ is joined to two vertices of $T$ in $G$ if every vertex $y \in Y$ is adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices $u, v \in T$.

results.title: Erdős–Faudree triangle conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the following holds for all sufficiently large $n$: every simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with more than $n^2/4$ edges contains a triangle $T$ and a set $Y$ of vertices, each adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices of $T$, with $|Y| > (1/2 - \varepsilon)n$.

results.title: Negation of the Erdős–Faudree triangle conjecture
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that the Erdős–Faudree triangle conjecture fails, that is, that it is not the case that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with more than $n^2/4$ edges contains a triangle $T$ and a set $Y$ of vertices, each adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices of $T$, with $|Y| > (1/2 - \varepsilon)n$.

results.title: Book lower bound for Erdős Problem 1034
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the following holds for all sufficiently large $n$: every simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with more than $n^2/4$ edges contains a triangle $T$ and a set $Y$ of vertices, each adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices of $T$, with $|Y| \ge (1/6 - \varepsilon)n$.

results.title: Ma–Tang upper bound for Erdős Problem 1034
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the following holds for all sufficiently large $n$: there is a simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with more than $n^2/4$ edges such that for every triangle $T$ of $G$, every set $Y$ of vertices each adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices of $T$ satisfies $|Y| \le (2 - \sqrt{5/2} + \varepsilon)n$.

results.title: $K_4$-free upper bound for Erdős Problem 1034
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the following holds for all sufficiently large $n$: there is a simple graph $G$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no $K_4$ and has more than $n^2/4$ edges, such that for every triangle $T$ of $G$, every set $Y$ of vertices each adjacent in $G$ to two distinct vertices of $T$ satisfies $|Y| \le (2\sqrt{3} - 3 + \varepsilon)n$.

results.title: The Erdős–Faudree triangle conjecture is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every simple graph on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with more than $n^2/4$ edges contains a triangle $T$ and a set of more than $(1/2 - \varepsilon)n$ vertices, each adjacent to two distinct vertices of $T$.

results.title: Single-locus model under random union of gametes
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A single locus under random union of gametes: allele frequencies `p` on a finite allele set and symmetric genotypic values `g a b` (the mean phenotype of genotype `{a, b}`).

results.title: Population mean genotypic value at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The population mean genotypic value `μ = ∑ p_a p_b g(a, b)`.

results.title: Fisher's average effect of an allele at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fisher's average effect of allele `a`: `α a = ∑_b p_b g(a, b) - μ`.

results.title: Dominance deviation at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dominance deviation `δ a b = g(a, b) - μ - α a - α b`.

results.title: Genetic variance at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genetic variance `V_G = ∑ p_a p_b (g(a, b) - μ)²`.

results.title: Additive variance at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The additive variance `V_A = 2 ∑ p_a α_a²`.

results.title: Dominance variance at a single locus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dominance variance `V_D = ∑ p_a p_b δ_{ab}²`.

results.title: Average effects are centred
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Average effects are centred: `∑ p_a α_a = 0`.

results.title: Dominance deviations are orthogonal to every allele
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dominance deviations are orthogonal to every allele: `∑_b p_b δ_{ab} = 0`.

results.title: Fisher decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Fisher decomposition of the genetic variance: `V_G = V_A + V_D`.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the single-locus additive variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The additive variance is nonnegative.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the single-locus dominance variance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The dominance variance is nonnegative.

results.title: The additive fit is least squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The additive fit is least squares (Fisher definition of average effects): every additive fit `c + h a + h b` has mean squared error at least `V_D`, the error of `μ + α a + α b`.

results.title: Mean product of genotypic values of two relatives
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean product of genotypic values of two non-inbred relatives that share `0`, `1`, `2` alleles identical by descent with probabilities `k₀, k₁, k₂`: given the IBD state, the non-shared alleles are independent draws from `p`.

results.title: Covariance between relatives
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Covariance between relatives at one locus (Fisher 1918; in the IBD form of Falconer and Mackay ch. 9): for IBD probabilities summing to one, `E[G_X G_Y] - μ² = (k₁ / 2 + k₂) V_A + k₂ V_D`, i.e. `2φ V_A + Δ V_D` with kinship `φ = k₁ / 4 + k₂ / 2` and `Δ = k₂`.

results.title: Cockerham–Kempthorne variance components
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Cockerham–Kempthorne variance components up to order `n`: `V i j = V_{A^i D^j}` is the component of `i` additive and `j` dominance factors (`V 1 0 = V_A`, `V 0 1 = V_D`, `V 2 0 = V_AA`, …). They are nonnegative, there is no `(0, 0)` component, and the genetic covariance of relatives with `2φ` and `Δ` is `∑_{i, j ≤ n} (2φ)^i Δ^j V i j`. This structure is the stated representation; it is proved for one locus by…

results.title: Genetic covariance of relatives in Cockerham form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The genetic covariance of relatives with coefficients `2φ = twoPhi` and `Δ = Δ`.

results.title: Additive variance of the Cockerham components
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The additive variance `V_A = V 1 0` (zero if `n = 0`).

results.title: Falconer's estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Falconer's estimator under the ACE model, in covariance form: monozygotic twins have `2φ = Δ = 1`, dizygotic twins (full sibs) `2φ = 1/2`, `Δ = 1/4`, and both share the same common-environment covariance `C`; the estimator is `2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ)`.

results.title: Falconer's estimator in terms of Cockerham components
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Falconer's estimator is `V_A` plus the non-additive components weighted by `2 (1 - 2^{-i} 4^{-j})` (derived from Cockerham's coefficients).

results.title: Phantom heritability inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The phantom-heritability inequality in covariance form: `V_A ≤ 2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ)`.

results.title: Equality case of the phantom heritability inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Equality holds iff every non-additive component of order `≤ n` vanishes.

results.title: Phantom heritability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Phantom heritability on the correlation scale (Zuk et al. 2012): with phenotypic variance `V_P > 0`, the narrow-sense heritability `V_A / V_P` is at most the ACE estimate `2 (r_MZ - r_DZ)`, where `r = Cov / V_P`.

results.title: Single-locus model as Cockerham components
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The one-locus model as Cockerham components of order `1`: `V 1 0 = V_A`, `V 0 1 = V_D`, `V 1 1 = 0`.

results.title: Single-locus covariance between relatives in Cockerham form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The one-locus covariance between relatives is the Cockerham form of `toComponents`.

results.title: One-locus phantom heritability, unconditional
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With monozygotic twins (`k₂ = 1`), dizygotic twins (`k = (1/4, 1/2, 1/4)`) and a common environment `C`, `2 (Cov_MZ - Cov_DZ) = V_A + (3/2) V_D`.
